nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $f \in A[X]$ be a polynomial, and let $\alpha$ be the image of $X$ in $A[X]/(f)$. Then the image in $A[X]/(f)$ of the constant coefficient $f(0)$ of $f$ lies in the principal ideal $(\alpha)$.
nodes.title: The constant coefficient lies in the ideal generated by the adjoined root

nodes.title: Totally ramified extensions are generated by an Eisenstein uniformizer

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, let $f \in A[X]$ be a monic polynomial of positive degree that is Eisenstein with respect to $\mathfrak m$, and let $\alpha$ be the image of $X$ in $A[X]/(f)$. Then $\alpha$ is an irreducible element of $A[X]/(f)$.
nodes.title: The adjoined root of an Eisenstein polynomial over a DVR is irreducible

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and let $f \in A[X]$ be a monic polynomial of positive degree that is Eisenstein with respect to $\mathfrak m$. Then $A[X]/(f)$ is a discrete valuation ring.
nodes.title: Adjoining a root of an Eisenstein polynomial to a DVR gives a DVR

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, let $f \in A[X]$ be a monic polynomial of positive degree that is Eisenstein with respect to $\mathfrak m$, and let $\alpha$ be the image of $X$ in $A[X]/(f)$. If $A[X]/(f)$ is a local ring, then its maximal ideal is the principal ideal $(\alpha)$.
nodes.title: The maximal ideal of an Eisenstein extension of a DVR is generated by the root

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and let $f \in A[X]$ be a monic polynomial of positive degree that is Eisenstein with respect to $\mathfrak m$. Then $A[X]/(f)$ is a local ring.
nodes.title: An Eisenstein extension of a DVR is local

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, let $f \in A[X]$ be a monic polynomial of positive degree that is Eisenstein with respect to $\mathfrak m$, and let $\alpha$ be the image of $X$ in $A[X]/(f)$. Then the principal ideal $(\alpha)$ of $A[X]/(f)$ is a maximal ideal.
nodes.title: The adjoined root of an Eisenstein polynomial generates a maximal ideal

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, let $f \in A[X]$ be a polynomial of positive degree that is Eisenstein with respect to $\mathfrak m$, and let $\alpha$ be the image of $X$ in $A[X]/(f)$. Then the ideal of $A[X]/(f)$ generated by the image of $\mathfrak m$ is contained in the principal ideal $(\alpha)$.
nodes.title: The maximal ideal of a DVR maps into the ideal of an Eisenstein root

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and let $f \in A[X]$ be a polynomial of positive degree that is Eisenstein with respect to $\mathfrak m$. Then $\mathfrak m$ is the principal ideal generated by the constant coefficient $f(0)$ of $f$.
nodes.title: The constant term of an Eisenstein polynomial generates the maximal ideal of a DVR

nodes.summary: Let $A \subseteq B$ be an extension of discrete valuation rings with $B$ finite over $A$ and the inclusion a local homomorphism, and let $K \subseteq L$ be their fraction fields, with the maps $A \to B \to L$ and $A \to K \to L$ agreeing. If a uniformizer $\pi$ of $B$ satisfies $B = A[\pi]$, then the ramification index of the maximal ideal of $B$ over $A$ equals $[L : K]$.

nodes.title: An Eisenstein generating uniformizer gives total ramification

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, let $f \in A[X]$ be a monic polynomial that is Eisenstein with respect to $\mathfrak m$, and let $\alpha$ be the image of $X$ in $A[X]/(f)$. Then $\alpha$ lies in every maximal ideal of $A[X]/(f)$.
nodes.title: Every maximal ideal of an Eisenstein extension of a DVR contains the root

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a local integral domain with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, let $f \in A[X]$ be a monic polynomial of positive degree that is Eisenstein with respect to $\mathfrak m$, and let $\alpha$ be the image of $X$ in $A[X]/(f)$. Then $\alpha \neq 0$.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
